abstract: A small library of indanesulfonamides was screened for the inhibition of the human carbonic anhydrase (CA, EC 4.2.1.1) isoforms involved in neuronal excitation, that is, isoforms VII, XII and XIV. These CA isoforms are becoming interesting target for the design of agents useful for the treatment of epilepsy. The inhibition pattern of these indanesulfonamide compounds towards these three isoforms was excellent, with many nanomolar inhibitors detected (K(I)s in the range of 0.78-10 nM against hCA VII; 0.32-56 nM against hCA XII, and 0.47-1030 nM against hCA XIV, respectively). The maximal electroshock seizure (MES) test performed on mice showed a good anticonvulsant activity for some compounds which protected the mice against convulsions in the 50-62.5% range at a dose of 50 mg/kg. In parallel, the blood-brain barrier passive permeation of these sulfonamides was also estimated by using a computational approach.
authors: Thiry A, Rolin S, Vullo D, Frankart A, Scozzafava A, Dogné JM, Wouters J, Supuran CT, Masereel B.
title: Indanesulfonamides as carbonic anhydrase inhibitors and anticonvulsant agents: structure-activity relationship and pharmacological evaluation.
